action: Grey light. Dressed for work, a cardigan under the jacket. The envelope from Chapter 3 is still under the fruit bowl.
They know line one of the back flap: 'The Albion, by the station - until Friday.' They have not read past it. Daniel is in the city.
Coffee ritual performed with aggressive precision; the spoon hits the mug harder than it needs to.
Lift the fruit bowl, check the envelope is fully covered, set the bowl down; lift it and check again.
Sarah lets herself in by the back door, fills the kettle without asking where anything is; she has brought a box of her own tea.
Sarah asks where she can keep the tea; they point at the empty middle dresser drawer; she puts the box in.
Sarah reaches past the fruit bowl for a spoon; her sleeve nudges the bowl and a corner of the envelope shows; she pushes the bowl back over it without looking down. They watch. Neither says anything.
Sarah asks about the weekend; they make a joke about her new project that is too quick and lands wrong. Sarah: 'You don't have to do that.' She goes out to wait by the car.
cost: They hear the joke land wrong; regret it immediately and do not take it back; Sarah leaves to wait by the car.

action: Alone for thirty seconds: the envelope comes out from under the fruit bowl and goes into the middle drawer, on top of Sarah's tea.
The key comes off the keyring for the first time in nine years; the drawer is locked; the key goes back on the ring.
Drive to work in silence; the radio is on.
cost: Neither of them hears the radio; they do not look out of the window once.

action: Find the hotel's website on their phone; do not call; clear the browser history.
cost: Clearing the browser history takes longer than reading the letter would have.
